thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Automatic failover triggered for traffic-manager:global -> us-east-1 due to elevated 5xx/latency from us-west-2 egress. Alert group: egress-dns-errors. Severity: P2. @maya (oncall) paged by pagerduty :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing partial client timeouts and retries. lowering TTL and assessing failover healthchecks now.

sanjay: I'm looking at route analytics and seeing rapid health-check toggles for us-west-2-b egress proxies. connection errors look like NXDOMAIN and some upstream TCP resets.

lia: +1. DNS NXDOMAIN spike from our egress-resolver pool starting ~06:12 UTC. stack traces show retry storms in frontends. grabbing dns analytics.

ops-bot: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/egress-failover. Suggested play: 1) pause automated failover, 2) lower public DNS TTL to 30s, 3) drain region after manual weight shift.

maya (oncall): Doing step 2 now. changing traffic-manager ttl -> 30s.

sanjay: Copy. Also I'm seeing a fliploop: health-checks go unhealthy -> traffic shifts -> health checks come back -> traffic shifts back and on and on. That causes state thrash and customer-facing errors. We should disable automatic flipback for this run.

lia: Logs (excerpt):
```
[06:12:18] upstream: dns query failed: NXDOMAIN from resolver-3.us-west-2
[06:12:19] egress-proxy us-west-2-b: 502 Bad Gateway -> upstream conn reset
[06:12:22] health-check: probe failed (conn timeout)
```

network-eng: Looks like an AZ-specific NAT/transit issue. I'm tracing BGP flips on the cloud edge for us-west-2-b; routes are being withdrawn briefly which would explain both TCP resets and intermittent NXDOMAIN if resolver frontends are behind that path.

maya (oncall): Proposed mitigation: 1) pause automated routing policy (disable health-check-triggered failover), 2) manually set traffic-manager weight: us-west-2=0, us-east-1=100 for affected prefix, 3) drain us-west instances (graceful). Anyone object?

sanjay: +1. Manual weight change in progress. Command: `redwoodctl traffic-manager set-weight global us-west-2 0 --reason "incident 1758003000"`

ops-bot: Executing traffic-manager change as requested by maya. Please monitor in console.

lia: After weight change, I'm seeing error rate drop in frontends within 2m. Latency normalizing. But note: some clients still have cached DNS pointing to us-west. That's why TTL lowering was important.

maya (oncall): Initiating graceful drain of us-west-2-b egress fleet: `kubectl -n infra rollout pause deployment/egress-proxy-us-west-2-b; kubectl annotate pod <...> redwood/drain=true` -> upgrading infra nodes and cycling NAT gateway attachments.

network-eng: I'm replacing the suspect ENI and forcing the route tables to refresh. Also asking cloud provider to examine edge flaps at their POP.

sanjay: Quick note: do not re-enable auto failback until provider confirms route stability + we've observed 15m stable metrics. Otherwise we'll flip again.

maya (oncall): Customer impact summary (initial): 06:10-06:28 UTC: ~8% of production requests returned 5xx or timed out for customers routed primarily through us-west-2-b. Top affected tenants: AcmeCorp (paying prod), DataQuery Inc (ingest jobs). Noting SLO breach window potential. Sending notifications to account teams.

lia: Creating an internal incident page with metric graphs and sample traces: https://internal.redwood/incident/1758003000

maya (oncall): Handoff plan: I'll stay until us-west looks healthy and providers confirm. If need be, @lia you take over at 07:05 UTC. Steps for handoff: confirm traffic-manager weight=100 us-east, check DNS TTL is lowered, confirm pool nodes drained, verify no health-check flips for 15m.

lia: Acknowledged. I'll prepare post-incident action items: (1) failover hysteresis change to avoid immediate flipback, (2) add NAT/ENI monitoring alert with faster pager, (3) test plan for planned region drains.

ops-bot: Pagerduty incident created: PD-1758003000. Severity set to Sev2.

network-eng: Cloud provider says they observed transient routing flap at their edge affecting 1 AZ between 06:09-06:13 UTC. They've opened ticket CP-98765 and are investigating root cause at their POP.

sanjay: Monitoring: 06:18–06:35 traffic to us-west-2 dropped to near 0; client errors decreased correspondingly. Rolling window 5m error rate is back to baseline.

maya (oncall): Status update @45m in: Traffic stabilized, manual weight remains set (us-east serving), provider ticket open. I'm going to leave the region drained and keep automated failback disabled for now.

lia: I'll take over active monitoring. Handoff check: traffic-manager weights locked, postmortem owner assigned?

maya (oncall): Assigning postmortem to @sanjay. He'll collect timeline + infra changes. Lia will own action items and runbook updates.

sanjay: Will do. Initial timeline and artifacts: metrics snapshot, logs, `redwoodctl` commands executed, cloud provider ticket.

incident-bot: Incident status: ongoing -> mitigation in place. Please update the incident page with any new information. :white_check_mark:

lia: Noting customer comms draft: "We observed a regional networking issue impacting a subset of traffic to us-west causing transient errors. Traffic was manually shifted and affected hosts drained. We will follow up with a postmortem." Sending to comms for review.

maya (oncall): Leaving handoff to @lia at 07:05 UTC. If anything spikes, page pagerduty->oncall.

lia: Taking over. Monitoring dashboards look stable at 07:05. Will keep auto-failback disabled until CP confirms root-cause and we validate 30m of stability.

network-eng: Provider updated CP-98765: edge-switchover triggered due to a fabric maintenance job; they underestimated blast radius. Requesting postmortem from provider.

lia: Closing update for now. Next steps: (1) confirm provider postmortem, (2) revert DNS TTL after stability, (3) implement hysteresis in traffic-manager to prevent fliploops, (4) schedule soak test for planned AZ drains.

sanjay: Postmortem kickoff created and assigned.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring (no active mitigation changes). Keep the thread updated if any regressions occur.

maya (oncall): Thanks team. Good coordination. :thumbsup:
